content_voiceover: This is the PhALLCON trial, a global phase three study that earned ponatinib a new frontline indication, marked here with the red new indication flag. The question was whether frontline ponatinib beats imatinib when each is combined with reduced intensity chemotherapy in adults with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL. Two hundred forty five patients were randomized in a two to one fashion, one hundred fifty four to ponatinib at thirty milligrams daily, dropping to fifteen after achieving MRD negative complete remission, and seventy eight to imatinib at six hundred milligrams daily, both layered onto reduced intensity chemotherapy. The primary outcome was MRD negative complete remission at the end of induction, defined as BCR-ABL1 by MR4, meaning point zero one percent or less. The result favored ponatinib decisively, thirty four point four percent achieving MRD negative CR compared to just sixteen point seven percent with imatinib, a statistically significant absolute risk difference of eighteen percentage points with a p value of point zero zero two. For boards, remember this trial name, PhALLCON, established ponatinib as the preferred frontline TKI partner in Ph positive ALL when paired with reduced intensity chemotherapy rather than the older imatinib backbone.
keypoints: PhALLCON: phase 3, ponatinib vs imatinib + reduced-intensity chemo
Newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL, N=245, 2:1 randomization
Primary endpoint: MRD-negative CR at end of induction
keypoint_voiceover: PhALLCON is the trial to know here: ponatinib plus reduced intensity chemotherapy roughly doubled the MRD negative complete remission rate compared to imatinib, thirty four percent versus seventeen percent, and that's what earned ponatinib its new frontline approval in Philadelphia positive ALL.
